result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: The current version of §415.20 remains in effect through December 31, 2026.
claims.quote: This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027, and as of that date is repealed.

claims.claim: For a person specified in §416.60, 416.70, 416.80 or 416.90, subdivision (b) permits substituted service if the summons and complaint cannot with reasonable diligence be personally delivered.
claims.quote: If a copy of the summons and complaint cannot with reasonable diligence be personally delivered to the person to be served, as specified in Section 416.60, 416.70, 416.80, or 416.90, a summons may be served by leaving a copy of the summons and complaint

claims.claim: The first step is to leave a copy at the dwelling house, usual place of abode, usual place of business, or usual mailing address other than a USPS post office box.
claims.quote: leaving a copy of the summons and complaint at the person’s dwelling house, usual place of abode, usual place of business, or usual mailing address other than a United States Postal Service post office box

claims.claim: The copy is left in the presence of a competent household member or a person apparently in charge of the office, place of business or qualifying mailing address.
claims.quote: in the presence of a competent member of the household or a person apparently in charge of their office, place of business, or usual mailing address other than a United States Postal Service post office box

claims.claim: That person must be at least 18.
claims.quote: at least 18 years of age

claims.claim: That person must be informed of the contents.
claims.quote: who shall be informed of the contents thereof

claims.claim: The second step is to mail a copy of both papers by first-class mail with postage prepaid.
claims.quote: and by thereafter mailing a copy of the summons and of the complaint by first-class mail, postage prepaid

claims.claim: The mailing goes to the person to be served at the place where the copy was left.
claims.quote: to the person to be served at the place where a copy of the summons and complaint were left.

claims.claim: Service is deemed complete on the 10th day after mailing.
claims.quote: Service of a summons in this manner is deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing.

claims.claim: In the ordinary civil case described, the summons must direct the defendant to file a written responsive pleading with the court.
claims.quote: (3) A direction that the defendant file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: Subdivision (a) qualifies its requirements with “Except as otherwise required by statute”.

claims.claim: The summons directs filing within 30 days after service on the defendant.
claims.quote: within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: The starting event is service, not the mailing itself.

claims.claim: In computing time, the first day is excluded.
claims.quote: The time in which any act provided by law is to be done is computed by excluding the first day

claims.claim: The last day is included unless it is a holiday.
claims.quote: and including the last, unless the last day is a holiday, and then it is also excluded.

claims.claim: The replacement version becomes operative January 1, 2027.
claims.quote: (e) This section shall become operative on January 1, 2027.

claims.claim: Under the replacement subdivision (b), a party shows reasonable diligence through good-faith attempts at personal delivery.
claims.quote: For purposes of this subdivision, a party shows reasonable diligence by attempting personal delivery of the summons and complaint, in good faith, on at least three occasions on three different days at three different times.

claims.claim: There must be at least three such occasions.
claims.quote: on at least three occasions

claims.claim: The attempts must span three different days.
claims.quote: on three different days

claims.claim: The attempts must be at three different times.
claims.quote: at three different times.

claims.claim: In a consumer-debt collection action, at least one attempt must be at the person's dwelling place or usual place of abode, subject to the stated address condition.
claims.quote: In an action to collect “consumer debt,” as defined in Section 1788.2 of the Civil Code, at least one of the service attempts shall be made at the dwelling place or usual place of abode of the person to be served

claims.claim: That requirement applies if the dwelling place or usual place of abode is known or could be determined with reasonable effort.
claims.quote: provided that the dwelling place or usual place of abode is known or could be determined with reasonable effort.

claims.claim: USPS first-class mail remains an option in 2027.
claims.quote: by United States Postal Service first-class mail, Priority Mail with tracking, or Certified Mail with return receipt requested, with postage prepaid

claims.claim: Priority Mail with tracking is a 2027 option.
claims.quote: Priority Mail with tracking

claims.claim: Certified Mail with return receipt requested is a 2027 option.
claims.quote: Certified Mail with return receipt requested

claims.claim: In 2027, service is still deemed complete on the 10th day after mailing.
claims.quote: Service of a summons in this manner is deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing.

flags.text: On January 1, 2027, subdivision (b) specifies the diligence attempts, adds the conditional home-attempt requirement for consumer-debt actions, and expands the mailing options. The completion date does not change.
The draft's citation list omits CCP-12, the provided source for the time-computation rule.

result.summary: Both versions measure completion from mailing: service is complete on the 10th day after mailing, and the summons's 30-day response period runs from service. The draft distinguishes the 2027 changes from the rules in effect on November 19, 2026.
